facts.text: On this date in 1964, Nikita Khrushchev was ousted while on vacation — the only Soviet leader removed by his own Politburo while still alive.
On this date in 1947, Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier. He named his Bell X-1 aircraft 'Glamorous Glennis' after his wife.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire United States west of the Mississippi River.
Monaco has a higher density of millionaires per capita than any country on Earth — roughly one in three residents qualifies.
The city of Istanbul straddles two continents, but its European side holds only about 3% of Turkey's land while housing a third of its economy.
On this day in 1947, Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier — the same week the Dow Jones closed below 180. The index has since risen over 230x.
On this day in 1964, Khrushchev was ousted. Soviet state media reported nothing unusual. Western markets barely flinched — Cold War risk was already priced in.
The entire U.S. housing market is worth roughly $47 trillion. That's more than the GDP of the U.S., China, and Germany combined.
Berkshire Hathaway's Class A share once traded for $700,000 each — Buffett never split it deliberately, to deter short-term traders.
The tulip mania peak in 1637 lasted just days. A single Semper Augustus bulb fetched 10x a skilled craftsman's annual wage before the market collapsed in hours.
On this date in 1947, Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier — but the sonic boom he created technically never stopped. It trailed behind his jet as a continuous shockwave cone, not a single event.
On this date in 1968, Apollo 7 astronauts became the first humans to broadcast live from space. The signal traveled 354 km to Earth faster than the light from a candle reaches your eye.
Your skeleton is not the rigid scaffold it appears. Bone is a living tissue that completely replaces itself every decade, meaning your current skeleton is younger than most of your memories.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly 10 million tons on Earth's surface.
The mantis shrimp sees the world through 16 types of photoreceptors. Humans have 3. It does not see richer color — its brain processes hues so fast it essentially reads light like a barcode.

On this day in 1066, Harold II died at Hastings — ending Anglo-Saxon England forever. The battle lasted one afternoon. A millennium of language, law, and culture pivoted on a single October Wednesday.

On this day in 1947, Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier over the Mojave. The aircraft was named 'Glamorous Glennis' after his wife. He was 24, still healing from two broken ribs he'd hidden from his commanders.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 26 years before the transcontinental railroad was completed. You could theoretically fax a document across a wire before you could cross America by train.
Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire by roughly 300 years. When Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325, Oxford dons had already been lecturing for two centuries.
Napoleon was born closer in time to the moon landing than to the fall of the Western Roman Empire. He felt ancient. He wasn't.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home you cannot return to — or that never existed. Untranslatable into English, which says something about English.
On this date in 1066, the Battle of Hastings introduced French into English at sword-point. A third of the modern English lexicon arrived with Norman conquerors.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word for the look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The Guinness-listed most succinct word ever recorded.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Another Koenig coinage — proof that naming a feeling is the fastest way to make millions of strangers feel less alone.

On this date in 2013, the FBI seized ~26,000 BTC from Silk Road — then the largest Bitcoin seizure ever. The coins were later auctioned by the U.S. Marshals Service in lots, with Tim Draper winning 29,656 BTC across multiple sales.
On Oct 14, 2020, Filecoin's mainnet launched after raising $257M in a 2017 ICO — the longest gap between fundraise and launch of any major crypto project at the time.
Bitcoin's script language is deliberately not Turing-complete. Satoshi removed loop opcodes before launch to prevent denial-of-service attacks via infinite loops clogging nodes.
The Ethereum genesis block contains a hidden message in its extra data field: a Times of London headline — mirroring Satoshi's own embedding in Bitcoin's block 0, a deliberate homage.

MakerDAO's "Black Thursday" in March 2020 saw ETH price drop so fast that some Vault liquidations cleared for $0 DAI — winning bidders acquired collateral for free due to network congestion delaying competing bids.

On this date in 2003, Geoffrey Hinton's team published the paper introducing Contrastive Divergence, the training trick that made deep Boltzmann machines practical and quietly set the stage for the 2012 deep learning breakout.

On this date in 2015, Elon Musk, Sam Altman, and others filed OpenAI's incorporation papers — a nonprofit explicitly designed to counter Google's AI dominance, a mission structurally abandoned within four years.

AlphaFold 2 predicted protein structures for virtually every known organism — roughly 200 million proteins — at a cost estimated below $10 million, a task that would have taken wet-lab science thousands of years at 1990s throughput.
The GPT-4 training run is estimated to have consumed around 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US homes — before a single user query was served.
RLHF, the technique that made large language models feel conversational, was originally developed in 2017 to teach robots to backflip from human preference labels, not to align text generation.
